stronger_left_out.name: Bornholm

stronger_left_out.name: Kojonup
stronger_left_out.reason: For: Australia's South West has a Kojonup destination page and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany itinerary calls it a 'popular stop'; the town has The Kodja Place and the Military Barracks museum. | Objection: Against: its one real draw, The Kodja Place, is a separate candidate, so the town would be a wrapper beside its own attraction (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); a service stop on Albany Highway rather than a base.

stronger_left_out.name: Michaelmas Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: a nature reserve island with no visitor access; seen only from Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.

stronger_left_out.name: Bald Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: an offshore nature reserve with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.

stronger_left_out.name: King George Sound
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 3: a body of water, seen from the places on its shore (Middleton Beach, Emu Point, Torndirrup lookouts, Princess Royal Fortress); no counted source names it as a place to go, and whale-watching tours on it are operators.

stronger_left_out.name: Wilson Inlet
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (paddling, kayak and canoe hire, fishing, the 12 km Wilson Inlet Heritage Trail to Crusoe Beach, inlet cruises). Case for: a counted source and a range of things to do. Case against: rule 3, a water body whose visitor points are Ocean Beach (kept) and Denmark's riverfront; the Heritage Trail might be the better spot. | Objection: A 20 km water body has no single visitor point; overlaps Ocean Beach.

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Riche
stronger_left_out.reason: Re-looked: one counted source, Visit Albany's (amazingalbany.com.au) nature-based camping page, which names Cape Riche as a caretaker-run campground; the City of Albany camping page agrees. Case for: a remote cape for fishing, swimming, snorkelling, headland rock walks and Mount Melville. Case against: named only as a campground, no source describes a sight; one source. | Objection: A campground listing is not a visitor 'See' entry; mostly anglers and campers.

stronger_left_out.name: Eclipse Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island with no public access, seen from Torndirrup's lookouts; no counted source names it as a place to go.

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Melville
stronger_left_out.reason: For: a summit with an observation tower ('the Spark Plug') and walk trails over Albany, Princess Royal Harbour and King George Sound; Lonely Planet carried a 'Mt Melville Lookout Tower' sight (seen in search only; the page now redirects). | Objection: Against: no counted source could be opened (Visit Albany's walks and parks pages do not name it), reviewers report the upper stairs closed and trees blocking views; Mount Clarence and Mount Adelaide are Albany's promoted lookouts.

stronger_left_out.name: Breaksea Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island in King George Sound with no public access; seen from the Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.

stronger_left_out_note: The lowest kept spots score 0 views and 0 counted sources on the verdict file (HMAS Perth Wreck, Stony Hill: their counted sources were found by the judge on re-look, after scoring), so every left-out candidate with any views or any counted source is listed. Each has a concrete 'What qualifies' reason: no public access (offshore islands), a duplicate of a kept spot, an operator, accommodation or business, a body of water, outside the region, or (reviews) a marginal case for the owner. None is left out for want of a home.

benchmark.note: COVERAGE step 6's benchmarks are New Zealand places and do not apply to this Western Australia region. Region checks instead: the Great Southern headlines are kept and placed: Bluff Knoll, the Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk, The Gap and Natural Bridge, Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks, the National Anzac Centre (Princess Royal Fortress), Albany's Historic Whaling Station, Misery Beach, Castle Rock Granite Skywalk and Point Ann. Operators and vehicles are rejected in favour of their places (Albany Whale Tours, Whale Watch WA, WOW Wilderness EcoCruise, Kaarl Wirn and Albany Tours; the Bremer Canyon orca trips are in Bremer Bay's bio only). Accommodation and shops are rejected (caravan parks, The Lake House, Denmark Chocolate Company). Inaccessible islands are rejected (Michaelmas, Breaksea, Bald, Eclipse). A civic building is rejected (Albany Town Hall), a memorial is merged into its hill (Desert Mounted Corps, into Mount Clarence), and a road and a drive are not spots (Hamersley Drive rejected; Stirling Range Scenic Drive in review). Gateway towns whose draw is beyond them are standalone at low priority (Mount Barker, Bremer Bay) or the base of their destination (Walpole), never wrappers beside their attractions; Kojonup is in review for exactly that reason.
